question: What will the U.S. seasonally adjusted annual rate of total housing starts be for August 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: months immediately following a >=10% MoM decline in total starts SAAR (1990-2026) - median next-month change roughly +7%, ~2 of 3 such months rise, which off the 1,239k July base anchors ~1,325k. This world's own 2026 series shows the same whipsaw (Apr->May -18.2%, May->Jun +18.0%). Supporting the bounce: July permits 1,443k vs starts 1,239k (16.5% gap vs a typical 5-8%), SF permits 894k > SF starts 808k, MF permits 490k > MF starts 421k, and NAHB HMI ticked 34->35. Pulling the other way and why I sit below consensus (1.35-1.36M) and below the thin Kalshi implied median (~1,337): the 2026 trend is clearly down (Jan-Apr avg 1,452 vs May-Jul avg 1,284), mortgage rates near a 12-month high at ~6.67%, >9 months of new-home supply, TD expecting subdued building through H2, and a late-August Gulf tropical system over the upper Texas coast. Net: median 1,315, i.e. a partial rather than full retracement. The August reference month is 100% elapsed as of 2026-09-07, so this is pure measurement uncertainty on an unusually noisy series - hence tails kept wide rather than narrowed.

No Polymarket or Manifold contract was found by the harness title search.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: any Bloomberg/Reuters/Action Economics economist-poll median specifically for the August 2026 reference month; any advance or leaked August estimate; regional (Northeast/Midwest/South/West) August indicators; the Census 'authorized but not started' backlog figure for July 2026; any assessment quantifying construction days lost to the late-August Gulf system.

STALE-SOURCE WARNING: two items surfaced in search that are NOT about this question - an InvestingChannel piece dated 2026-09-06 reporting 'October' starts of 1.246M against an October 2024 comparison and a government shutdown (that is October 2025 data), and a Haver piece describing an August rebound to 1.575M from 1.404M with permits at 1.517M (that is August 2022). calls.reference_class: US total privately-owned housing starts SAAR in the month immediately following a >=10% month-over-month decline (1990-2026), applied to the July 2026 base of 1,239k

calls.reasoning: The August reference month is fully elapsed as of 2026-09-07; this is nowcast error on an already-realized figure, so the whole distribution is one-month-ahead estimation uncertainty. Anchor: July first print 1239 (SF 808, 5+ 421). Reference class = months following a >=8% MoM decline in HOUST since Jan-2023: all 8 such months rose, mean +7.7%, median +5.2%, implying ~1300-1335. Corroborating up: July permits 1443 far exceed starts, SF permits 894 vs SF starts 808, NAHB HMI ticked 34->35, sell-side consensus ~1350. Corroborating down: -13.5% YoY, SF starts at a near-3-year low, mortgage rates ~6.66%, HMI below 40 for 16 straight months, completions -16.8% YoY, and 2027 forecasts drifting to ~1.27-1.29M. I split these at ~1310 median: reversion is mechanical and well-evidenced, but the trend is genuinely downward, so I sit below the 1350 consensus and above pure persistence. Component build agrees (SF ~845 + 5+ ~460 + 2-4 ~13 = 1318). Spread from historical MoM dispersion (9-10% SD), not from confidence. Escapes priced small but nonzero: 995 is a -19.7% MoM print, worse than any decline in the sample; 1605 requires a ~+30% multifamily-driven spike (5+ starts have jumped that hard before, e.g. the 1609 print in May 2023). No market price obtained (Kalshi 429'd twice; no Polymarket/Manifold contract), so no market blending was done.
sources: https://www.census.gov/construction/nrc/current/index.html (Monthly New Residential Construction, July 2026, CB26-127, rel. 2026-08-18)

calls.reference_class: Months immediately following a >=8% month-over-month decline in the Census/HUD total privately-owned housing starts SAAR series (HOUST), Jan-2023 through Jul-2026 (n=8), combined with the unconditional distribution of one-month changes in the same series (n=42)

calls.reasoning: Prior from the trailing-12-month HOUST median (1,332) and, conditionally, from the class 'month after a >=8% MoM drop' (5 cases 2024-2026, all positive, median +6.3% -> ~1,317 from July's 1,239). Three independent strands push the center above a naive carry-forward of 1,239: July permits 1,443 vs starts 1,239 gives a starts/permits ratio of 0.86 against a 2026 average of 0.96; single-family 808k is a clear outlier below the 2026 SF mean of ~906k; and a SF/MF rebuild (SF ~860, 5+ ~450, 2-4 ~28) lands near 1,340. Mortgage rates were flat at 6.65-6.69% through August, NAHB HMI ticked UP to 35 (beat 33), and the hurricane season is below-normal with no identified August construction disruption. Offsetting: a real H2 downshift (May-Jul average 1,279 vs Jan-Apr 1,417) and a genuine single-family downtrend as builders work off completed inventory (35% cutting prices, HMI below 40 for 16 straight months). I set the median at 1,318 — at the conditional rebound base rate, deliberately below both the SF/MF decomposition (~1,340) and the thin Kalshi implied median (~1,340), discounting the latter for sub-$200-notional books and ask-capped mids. Dispersion stays wide: Census's own 90% CI on the monthly change routinely spans zero, and 2026 has printed +233 and -232 single-month swings.

calls.reference_class: Monthly U.S. total privately-owned housing starts SAAR (Census/HUD HOUST), trailing 12 months Aug-2025..Jul-2026, plus the conditional sub-class 'the month immediately following a >=8% month-over-month decline' over 2024-2026

calls.reasoning: August is 100% elapsed as of 2026-09-07; the figure is realized and only publication is pending, so the whole distribution is estimation uncertainty on a noisy series. Anchor: July first print 1,239 (SF 808, 5+ 421), the second-lowest post-pandemic reading. The conditional-rebound class puts the center at ~1,315. Three independent strands push slightly higher: the starts/permits ratio fell to 0.86 vs a 0.96 2026 average (0.96 x 1,443 permits = ~1,385); SF at 808 is ~100k below its own 2026 mean and SF is the low-variance component, while 5+ at 431 was already near its 452 mean, so the mechanical room to revert sits in SF; and first prints have run ~+16k above later revisions this year, while two of the three runs built their base rates on revised data. Two weak external anchors (a ~120-contract Kalshi ladder implying ~1.34M, and a soft ~1.30-1.35M sell-side consensus) also sit above the runs. Against that: a genuine H2 downshift (May-Jul 1,279 vs Jan-Apr 1,417), HMI 35 for a 16th straight month below 40, buyer traffic 23, 35% of builders cutting prices, 9+ months of supply, and rates flat near 6.66%. All three runs applied the rebound base rate and then discounted again for a trend already embedded in that class; correcting that double-count lands me at 1,325, modestly above all of them and still below both market and consensus.
calls.reconciliation: Runs clustered tightly (medians 1310/1315/1318) so the work was auditing shared assumptions, not splitting differences. Settled factually: (a) the conditional-rebound base rate - Run 1's 1990-2026 window (~2 of 3 rise) supersedes Runs 2/3's 'all positive' over n=5-8, but all three imply a central next-month change of +5 to +7% off 1,239; (b) the Kalshi contract exists and matches the resolution criteria - Runs 1 and 3 independently retrieved the same ladder and implied median ~1.34M, resolving Run 2's failed fetch, though ~120 contracts of lifetime volume and 6-9c spreads make it corroboration rather than an anchor; (c) Run 1's late-August Gulf tropical storm and Runs 2/3's 'no disruption found' are compatible, since the latter are dated early August, and one day in one sub-region is immaterial to a SAAR; (d) the vintage question - resolution is the first print, 1,239 is the base under either vintage, and Run 2's own +16k first-print-minus-revised gap means revised-vintage base rates tilt slightly low. Unsettled: whether a genuine sell-side consensus panel for August 2026 exists (Runs 1/2 cite ~1.30-1.35M via aggregators, Run 3 found none posted); I let it carry that uncertainty and used it only as weak corroboration. The one pure judgment call: all three runs took the conditional rebound and then shaded down for the same downtrend that is already inside the reference class. I judge that a double-count and moved the median to 1,325 - above all three members because the reconciled evidence (permits ratio, SF-specific outlier, first-print tilt, two above-consensus external anchors) puts it there, while still well below the 1,385 the permits ratio alone would imply, because the H2 downshift is real. Dispersion carried forward from Runs 2/3 unchanged; no narrowing is warranted when consensus forecasters have missed by 100k+ in 5 of 7 recent months.

disagreements.claim: Months following a >=8-10% MoM decline rise essentially always (Runs 2/3, n=5-8) vs ~2 of 3 of the time (Run 1, 1990-2026)
disagreements.verdict: Run 1's longer window wins; 'all positive' is small-sample. All windows agree the central next-month change is +5 to +7%, so the anchor of ~1,315 survives either way.

disagreements.claim: A sell-side consensus of ~1.30-1.35M exists for the August 2026 reference month
disagreements.verdict: Could not settle without web access. Runs 1/2 cite aggregator figures; Run 3 found no posted panel and warns TE's cell carries July forward. Used as weak evidence only.

disagreements.claim: A directly-matching traded market exists for this release
disagreements.verdict: Settled yes - Runs 1 and 3 independently retrieved the same Kalshi ladder (strikes 1.150-1.500M, ~120 contracts volume, implied median ~1.34M); Run 2's non-retrieval was an HTTP 429. Too thin to anchor on; contract terms do match the resolution source and reference month.

disagreements.claim: A late-August Gulf tropical system disrupted South-region construction
disagreements.verdict: Compatible with Runs 2/3, whose 'no storm' statements are dated early August. Effect on a seasonally adjusted annual rate from ~1 day in one sub-region is negligible; no adjustment made.

disagreements.claim: Base rates should be computed on the revised FRED series (Runs 2/3) vs first prints (Run 1 / the question's Background)
disagreements.verdict: Resolution is the first print. July's 1,239 is identical under both vintages, so the anchor is unaffected, but Run 2's own +16k mean first-print-minus-revised gap implies revised-vintage base rates tilt slightly low - a small upward nudge.

disagreements.claim: How far below the conditional-rebound base rate the median should sit for the 2026 downtrend
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks this; I take the reading I would bet on. The rebound class already contains trending periods, so shading below it double-counts the trend. Median moved to 1,325, above all three runs but still below both the permits-ratio implication (~1,385) and the observed market/consensus (~1.34M).
